newsitem.title: USA: USDA says no cotton referendum planned.
newsitem.headline: USDA says no cotton referendum planned.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Tuesday it would not hold a referendum on the 1990 amendments to the Cotton Research and Promotion Act, based on the small number of industry requests for one.

In a notice published in the Federal Register, the agency's Agriculture Marketing Service said it conducted a sign-up Jan 15 through April 14, giving the cotton industry an opportunity to request a referendum. A total of 1,223 responses from state producing groups and cotton importers were submitted to USDA.

That number fell far short of the required 10 percent of the 46,220 ballots cast by cotton producers and importers in a July 1991 referendum, USDA said. Agency regulations provide a referendum to be held only upon the request of 10 percent or more of the number of cotton producers voting in the most recent referendum.
